the question of how far the analyst is allowed to influence the patient's personality in the direction of his own values.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
psychoanalysis is not a therapy of a particular illness, but a therapy of the personality.

the analyst's responsibility for his patient's social integration is not only a necessary condition for the success of the treatment, but also a necessary condition for his own professional integrity.
the values and goals of psychoanalytic treatment are determined by the individual patient's needs and the analyst's ability to recognize them and to respond to them.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
psychoanalytic therapy should not aim at the patient's adaptation to his milieu, but at his adaptation to himself.
we should not be afraid of our own values, as long as they do not prevent the patient from achieving his own goals.
we have to learn to see the patient as a whole person, to understand the meaning of his suffering and his needs, to accept him as he is, and to help him to accept himself.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need a new approach to psychotherapy.
we should be aware that we are not only treating a disease but a human being.
we need to be more flexible in how we approach the treatment of our patients and to be aware of the different values and goals that may be present.
